case_name: Sony Ericsson P800 — MCU Firmware Image Analysis (2004)
source_dataset: Champlain College Digital Forensics Challenge — Mobile Phone Corpus
description: Forensic image of Sony Ericsson P800 MCU (microcontroller unit) flash memory (file mcu.bin, 4194304 bytes, SHA-256: 2b8054d66bf8c2f1178ed70038fd557d53ab121890f2225ad32cf4a31c8a4b34). File date 2004-09-21. Examination reveals this is a Sony Ericsson GSM protocol stack firmware binary. The file contains the device's baseband firmware: GSM radio stack processes (FrameTick, SIMRX, LH_RX, LH_TX, LLC, RLC, MPH), SIM management (UICC, SIMTOOL), data processes (SNDCP, PPP, RLPH), phonebook/PB management, and voicemail (VoiceNote). String analysis reveals only internal process name table and GSM stack identifiers. No user-generated content (SMS, contacts, call log, emails, images) was found accessible in this memory region. This is the MCU firmware layer, not the user data partition. ABSTAIN verdict: the artifact is structurally valid firmware, but contains no user data from which forensic intent can be inferred.
devil_advocate: N/A — verdict is ABSTAIN, refutation protocol not required.

artifacts.description: String analysis of mcu.bin reveals: GSM stack process table (FrameTick_High_Priority_Process, HW_ADC_Done_Process, SIMRX_Process, LH_RX_Process, LLC_Process, RLC_Uplink_Process, MPH_Process, CB_Process, MM_Process, GCC_Process, SM_Process, etc.), SIM/UICC management (SIMTOOL_Process, UICC_Process), data stack (SNDCP_Process, PPP_Process, RLPH_Process), audio (HW_SpeechEncoderDecoder_Process, VoiceNote_Process), and maintenance processes (GDFS_Server_Process, GDFS_Write_Process, GDFS_Erase_Process). DATA_LINKHANDLER present (GPRS data). No user content (contacts, SMS, call log, calendar) detected in string extraction. Firmware layer only.

Binary firmware analysis. Mixed binary data (ARM/RISC machine code) and ASCII process name strings. Binary regions consistent with compiled firmware code. No isolated high-entropy blocks suggesting embedded encrypted payloads. No executable shell code injection patterns. No user-partition data structures detected.

metadata.forensic_conclusion: Artifact is device firmware only — no user-generated evidence available for analysis
